data.title: DraftKings stock just lost 20%: the real story isn't the earnings miss
data.description:
DraftKings (DKNG) shares opened sharply lower on Friday after the sports betting giant reported its fiscal Q3 earnings that missed Wall Street estimates and lowered its full-year guidance as well.

Revenue came in at $1.329 billion versus expectations of about $1.39 billion, while adjusted losses were also deeper than analysts had forecast.

Investors reacted swiftly, wiping billions from DKNG’s market cap. But the headline numbers tell only part of the story.

The bigger question for shareholders is whether DraftKings is “deliberately” sacrificing near-term profitability to pursue a potentially much larger opportunity in prediction markets.

DraftKings earnings miss is a strategy reset

At first glance, DraftKings release gave investors plenty of reasons to hit the sell button. The firm’s adjusted EBITDA slipped into negative territory as spending accelerated.

Plus, management reduced its sales ($6.35 billion to $6.55 billion) and EBITDA outlook as well.

Yet, what stands out is not weak customer demand. Monthly unique payers came in up 13% to 41 million, and average revenue per user increased to $109.

Those are not metrics typically associated with a fading business.

Instead, DKNG is making a conscious decision to redirect significant resources toward Predictions – its rapidly expanding prediction-markets platform.

In other words, investors were not simply reacting to missed estimates.

They were reacting to the realization that DraftKings is entering a new investment cycle, one that could weigh on profits far longer than Wall Street previously anticipated.

Significance of Predictions for DKNG shares

The most revealing part of the earnings release was buried behind the disappointing guidance.

Management disclosed that more than 1.6 million customers have engaged with its new Predictions offering this year – while annualized prediction-market consumer volume reached $10.1 billion in October.

The company said it has already become the third-largest predictions exchange by total volume.

Those figures help explain why executives are willing to accept hundreds of millions of dollars in additional investment.

Prediction markets sit at the intersection of sports betting, financial markets, and event forecasting, opening an entirely new revenue stream beyond traditional wagering.

For investors, this changes the valuation debate. DraftKings can no longer be viewed solely as a sports betting operator.

Increasingly, the stock is becoming a bet on management's ability to build a dominant platform in an emerging market that remains largely untapped.

The challenge is that such opportunities are difficult to model, making near-term earnings visibility much lower.

What DraftKings stock investors should watch next?

The irony of this sell-off is that the earnings report may have strengthened the long-term bull case even as it damaged short-term sentiment.

DraftKings introduced 2027 revenue guidance of $7.35 billion to $7.75 billion and forecast adjusted EBITDA of $800 million to $1.0 billion despite continuing investment in Predictions.

That suggests management sees today's spending less as an expense and more as customer acquisition for a business it believes can become materially larger over time.

The market, however, is demanding proof before granting that benefit of the doubt.

Going forward, three metrics matter more than quarterly earnings beats or misses: growth in prediction-market users, the pace of trading volume expansion, and evidence that those customers can be monetized profitably.

If those indicators continue trending upward, this week's plunge could eventually look like a temporary reaction to transition costs.

If they stall, investors may conclude that DraftKings traded a highly profitable future for an expensive experiment. For now, Wall Street is voting with caution.

data.title: Micron stock rebounds 5% after huge selloff even as AI demand risks persist
data.description:
Micron Technology shares MU are recovering after Thursday’s sharp technology selloff, but questions remain over whether the memory-chip maker’s low valuation reflects an investment opportunity or the risk of a downturn in AI-related demand.

The stock gained 5.8% on Friday after plunging 17% in the previous session.

At Thursday’s closing price, Micron traded at just 3.7 times its estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, according to FactSet.

That valuation appears particularly low given expectations that the company will more than double its revenue and earnings in the current fiscal year, with further growth forecast for the following year.

However, memory-chip companies often trade at low earnings multiples near the peak of their cycles, when profits are elevated.

Micron's low valuation faces memory-cycle risks

The main concern is whether demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence servers could weaken sooner than expected.

The potential slowdown in data-centre construction following Democratic victories in the US midterm elections has raised questions about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.

A downturn in memory demand, previously expected in 2028 or later, could arrive earlier if data-centre investment slows.

Micron has some protection against this risk through long-term take-or-pay agreements covering more than 35% of its forecast revenue through 2030.

The contracts require customers to pay for agreed supplies, potentially reducing the impact of normal fluctuations in memory-chip supply and demand.

However, there are concerns that customers could seek to renegotiate these agreements during a downturn in AI spending.

Similar contracts across the semiconductor industry during the supply shortages caused by the Covid pandemic were later renegotiated to maintain customer relationships.

Micron has received close to $32 billion in cash deposits under its agreements, but the durability of the contracts remains an important consideration for investors.

Buybacks could support Micron shares

The company also has the option of using share repurchases to support its stock. Micron can begin major buybacks from December 9.

Barron's estimates the company could repurchase $100 billion of its shares during its current fiscal year, which ends in August 2027. That amount would represent more than 10% of its current market value.

The potential scale of the buyback programme could provide another factor for investors assessing the stock's valuation, although its execution will depend on the company's capital allocation decisions.

Analysts divided on AI infrastructure outlook

Analyst views on semiconductor valuations and AI spending remain mixed.

UBS analyst Nicolas Gaudois argues that valuations for Micron's South Korean peers, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, indicate that markets are already pricing in a downturn in memory prices in 2028.

He estimates a risk-reward profile for the two companies that implies 160% potential upside over the next 12 months against 30% downside.

Micron trades at only a slightly higher valuation than the South Korean companies, suggesting a broadly similar scenario.

Raymond James Chief Investment Officer Larry Adam also remains positive on AI infrastructure.

He believes some semiconductor and AI stocks are trading at discounts of around 30% to historical valuations and expects earnings growth to remain healthy.

He therefore favours gradually rebuilding exposure to technology and semiconductor stocks.

However, Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives has become more cautious.

He now expects 10% fewer data centres in his baseline forecast, with potential reductions reaching 15% to 20%.

He also expects Big Tech capital spending growth to peak in 2027, earlier than previously anticipated.

Ives believes AI infrastructure projects are more likely to face delays than outright cancellations.

His preference has consequently shifted towards software stocks over semiconductor companies.

data.title: Fed rate hike odds jump after October jobs report as officials signal more tightening
data.description:
Traders are increasing their bets on another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December after a stronger-than-expected October employment report showed that the US labor market remains resilient.

The chance of a December rate hike rose to 77%, up about 10 percentage points from Thursday, according to CME FedWatch data.

The repricing suggests investors are becoming increasingly concerned that the central bank may need to tighten monetary policy further rather than pause its rate increases.

Job report comes in hot

The Labor Department reported on Friday that US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double economists' expectations of 65,000.

The unemployment rate also declined to 4.1% from 4.2%, while average hourly earnings increased 0.4% month over month, marking their strongest monthly gain since January.

Labor Department revisions also added a total of 84,000 new jobs to the August and September totals.

The stronger labour market data pushed Treasury yields higher with the benchmark 10-year note rising four basis points to 4.88.

The latest numbers followed the Federal Reserve's decision last week to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged in a range of 3.75% to 4%, after raising it in September.

The October employment data have strengthened expectations that policymakers could resume tightening as they continue to battle inflation.

Fed officials signal more rate increases

Comments from several Federal Reserve officials this week have reinforced expectations that borrowing costs may need to move higher.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said on Thursday that monetary policy would need to become restrictive to bring inflation back to the central bank's 2% target.

"I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Hammack said.

She favored smaller and more frequent rate adjustments, arguing that a gradual approach would be less disruptive to households, businesses and financial markets.

She also warned that delayed action could allow inflation expectations to become entrenched.

Hammack, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, voted in favor of a rate hike last week.

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin echoed those concerns, saying inflation remained too high and was holding steady rather than declining.

"Inflation is too high. That means the path is pretty straightforward. The question, of course, is pace,” Barkin told CNBC.

New York Fed President John Williams struck a somewhat similar tone on Friday.

While acknowledging that inflation remains elevated, he suggested policymakers should assess incoming data before deciding on further action.

"Inflation is absolutely too high. It's been too high for too long," Williams said at a European Central Bank conference in Frankfurt.

The latest jobs figures have strengthened the case for higher borrowing costs, but the wage data offer a more complicated picture.

Although monthly earnings accelerated, annual wage growth stood at 3.1%, remaining below inflation for the seventh consecutive month.

Investors will continue monitoring inflation, employment and energy prices for clues about the Fed's next move.

data.title: Three consumer stocks worth buying after US midterm elections
data.description:
Consumer discretionary stocks have emerged as one of the market’s biggest winners in the wake of the US midterm elections.

This has been fuelled by easing inflation expectations, falling Treasury yields, and renewed optimism that the Federal Reserve may not need to keep monetary policy restrictive for as long as previously feared.

As investors rotate out of energy and other defensive corners of the market, strategist Todd Gordon believes a stronger outlook for consumer spending could create opportunities in select discretionary names.

Among his favorites are homebuilder Lennar, consumer-products powerhouse SharkNinja, and e-commerce giant Amazon.

Lennar: a housing play leveraged to lower rates

While homebuilders have spent much of the past two years navigating affordability challenges and elevated mortgage rates, Lennar could be one of the biggest beneficiaries if borrowing costs continue to retreat.

The company's fiscal Q3 earnings reflected the difficult operating environment.

Lennar reported adjusted earnings of $1.23 per share, while gross margins on home sales came in at 15.8%, highlighting ongoing pressure from pricing and incentives.

The company generated $8.0 billion in revenue and maintained a manageable homebuilding debt-to-capital ratio of 16.6%.

Despite weaker profitability, Todd Gordon sees attractive long-term potential in the stock because housing demand remains structurally strong.

Lennar has continued building homes through the downturn rather than dramatically cutting production, positioning it to capture demand when financing conditions improve.

The investment thesis is straightforward: if inflation continues to cool and mortgage rates move lower, many prospective buyers who were sidelined by affordability concerns could return to the market.

That would likely support higher order volumes and improved pricing power across the homebuilding industry.

For investors looking to capitalize on a consumer recovery tied to lower interest rates, Lennar offers a direct way to express that view.

SharkNinja: riding innovation and consumer strength

SharkNinja has quietly become one of the strongest growth stories in consumer discretionary, combining product innovation with impressive execution across multiple categories.

The company reported third-quarter net sales of approximately $1.98 billion, up 21.2% year over year, while adjusted EBITDA surged roughly 46% to a margin of 23.3%.

Management was confident enough in the momentum to raise its full-year 2026 outlook, citing strength across both domestic and international markets.

Cooking and beverage revenue jumped 36.6%, while beauty and home-environment sales climbed 45.8%.

Gordon's bullish stance centers on the idea that discretionary spending may accelerate if consumers receive relief from lower energy costs and moderating inflation.

When households spend less at the gas pump, they often have more flexibility for purchases such as kitchen appliances, beauty products, and household upgrades, all areas where SharkNinja has established powerful brands.

Unlike many retailers that depend heavily on discounting, SharkNinja's growth is increasingly being driven by new product launches and category expansion.

That combination of innovation, market share gains, and improving macroeconomic conditions makes the stock an appealing way to participate in a resurgence of consumer spending.

Amazon: a pullback creates a long-term opportunity

Amazon remains one of the largest consumer discretionary holdings in the market, but investor concerns over massive artificial intelligence and infrastructure spending have recently weighed on the stock.

Those concerns emerged despite a strong third-quarter report.

Amazon generated $201.9 billion in revenue, up 12% year over year, while operating income surged 61% to a record $28.1 billion.

AWS revenue accelerated 39% to $46 billion, marking its fastest growth in nearly five years.

The company's cloud backlog expanded to roughly $578 billion, underscoring the scale of demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and cloud services.

The market's hesitation stems from Amazon's enormous capital spending plans.

Management expects approximately $220 billion in capital expenditures during 2026, largely directed toward AI infrastructure and data centers.

For Gordon, however, that pullback looks more like an opportunity than a warning sign.

Investors buying Amazon today are gaining exposure not only to a dominant online retail platform, but also to a rapidly expanding cloud-computing business and a highly profitable advertising segment.

If the post-election economic environment supports consumer confidence while AI demand remains robust, Amazon could be positioned to benefit from multiple growth drivers simultaneously.

As market leadership broadens beyond technology and investors search for sectors poised to benefit from easing inflation pressures, these three consumer-focused companies stand out as compelling ways to play a potential comeback in US discretionary spending.

data.title: Why Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has been summoned by US lawmakers?
data.description:
Three Republican House committee chairmen have asked Nvidia Corp. Chief Executive Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing over his reported contacts with a businesswoman suspected of spying for China.

A recent New York Times report stated that US intelligence officials concluded that businesswoman Alice Huang, who had cultivated a close relationship with the Nvidia chief, was passing information to the Chinese government.

Huang asked to appear on Nov 18

Reps. Brian Mast of Florida, John Moolenaar of Michigan and Rick Crawford of Arkansas sent a letter dated Nov. 4 requesting that Huang brief their panels jointly on Nov. 18.

The lawmakers chair the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

They cited recent news reports raising “significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information.”

The letter asks Huang to discuss Nvidia’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and his interactions with Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data-center firm Megaspeed International.

However, the letter does not name a specific report.

Huang has been asked to accept the date or propose an alternative by Nov. 11.

The committees said Chinese infiltration and access to cutting-edge American technology remain core investigative priorities this Congress.

What are the allegations?

The New York Times reported last month that Alice Huang, a senior executive at Singapore-based data-center firm Megaspeed International, has been identified as a Chinese agent by the US intelligence.

The newspaper also said President Donald Trump was briefed on the matter but took no action.

Subsequent reporting revealed that officials in Taiwan and Singapore also shared concerns that she may have provided sensitive details related to Nvidia chips.

Singapore has denied sharing any such information.

The allegations come as Washington continues to tighten controls on high-end semiconductors that power artificial intelligence systems.

Nvidia recently even told its data center partners to reduce their exposure to Chinese customers, according to Financial Times.

As per the report, the chipmaking giant wants its data center clients to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese companies.

Nvidia maintains stance

Nvidia continues to say that Huang's interactions with the suspected Chinese agent were usual business meetings, typical for a chief executive dealing with customers.

Nvidia expressed confidence that US authorities would notify it if they viewed any individual as a threat to American industry.

“We’re confident that if the US government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," Nvidia has said.

The Chinese government previously dismissed the spying allegations as “groundless speculation.” Beijing has consistently rejected claims that it targets US technology firms through intelligence operations.

data.title: Airbnb stock analysis after boosting its revenue and profit guidance
data.description:
Airbnb stock jumped to its highest point since November 2021 after the company published strong financial results. It jumped to $193, up by 136% from its lowest point on record, with its valuation rising to over $110 billion. This rally may continue in the near future. 

Airbnb published strong financial results

ABNB stock continued its strong rally after releasing its third-quarter earnings report. This report showed that its revenue jumped by 19% to $4.9 billion, with its net income soaring by 38% to $1.9 billion. These numbers were better than what most analysts were expecting. 

Most notably, the company said that its free cash flow (FCF) rising by nearly 30% to $1.4 billion, with the gross booking value hitting $27.7 billion. These numbers showed that its revenue growth gained momentum, which is rare for a company of its size. 

The company also hinted that the growth will continue in the coming quarters, helped by its innovation. It now expects that its fourth-quarter revenue will jump to between $3.22 billion and $3.28 billion, up by between 16% and 18%. These metrics were better than the average estimate of $3.16 billion.

For the year, the company is expected to grow in the high teens, higher than what analysts were expecting. Analysts were expecting its annual revenue to come in at $14.18 billion. These are encouraging numbers for a company that has not made any acquisitions. 

Instead, the management has continued to innovate, including by allowing hotels to add their rooms to the platform. Thousands of boutique and independent hotels have already signed up so far. It has also added car rentals, which have become popular among users, and partnered with American Express. It also partnered with Meta Platform to use Muse agent.

Analysts have reacted positively to the earnings. Ygal Arounian, a Wedbush analyst, hiked his target from $200 to $237, suggesting a 40% upside. Shyam Patil of Susquehanna hiked the forecast from $200 to $220, while Rosenblatt increased it from $220 to $230. Other analysts who have upgraded the stock recently are from companies like Cantor Fitzgerald, Raymond James, and UBS Group.

Some of these analysts note that the strong growth will help to justify its relatively high valuation. Kyro datashows that the company has a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 32, which is higher than the sector median of 16.

Airbnb stock technical analysis

ABNB stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the ABNB stock bottomed at $149.5 in September and then started an uptrend. It formed an up-gap today after publishing its financial results.

The stock has moved above the 50-day and 100-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). It has also moved above the Supertrend indicator and the median line of the Andrews pitchfork tool.

The stock will likely continue rising in the coming days as investors target the key resistance level of $200. This view will be confirmed if it jumps above the intraday high of $193.

data.title: What next for the IAG share price after earnings?
data.description:
IAG share price wavered on Friday, reaching a high of 437p, its highest point since August 24, up by 13.7% from its lowest point this month. This performance happened after the company published its financial results, which showed that its business did well in the third quarter despite the ongoing challenges.

IAG reported strong financial results amid rising energy costs

IAG, the parent company of British Airways, reported a mixed earnings report today, November 6. The report said that its revenue rose by 4.5% in the September quarter to €9.3 billion as demand remained steady and prices continued rising.

These gains were offset by the rising jet fuel prices, which were caused by the ongoing US-Iran war. IATA data shows that the average jet fuel price jumped to $191.54 last week, up by 3.8% from the previous month. It has risen by 112% from the same period last year.

As a result, the company’s operating profit dropped by 15.9% to €1.72 billion, while the profit after tax fell to €1.23 billion. On the other hand, the profit after tax fell by 12.2% to €1.23 billion

These numbers brought the nine-month revenue to €25.8 billion. This performance led to a significant decline in its profit metrics, with the profit after tax dropping to €2.2 billion. 

The company’s main challenge is that the cost of fuel is rising, with analysts expecting the prices to remain at an elevated level for a while. On the positive side, unlike its American competitors like Delta and United Airlines, IAG uses fuel hedges, which helps to offset the volatility in the market. It is now 45% hedged for next year and the management expects the annual fuel costs to be €8.9 billion. 

Most importantly for investors, IAG increased its dividends by 10% and is in the final stages of implementing the €1.5 billion buyback it announced earlier this year. IAG normally announces its annual buyback plans in the first quarter of the year. The CEO said:

“Our strong yield performance in all our markets reflects robust ongoing customer demand for travel for our airline brands. For the quarter, we have achieved an operating margin before exceptional items of 17.7%, despite the very high price of jet fuel and a number of one-off disruption events, clearly demonstrating the quality of our business.”

IAG share price technical analysis 

IAG stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the IAG stock price has remained in a narrow range in the past few weeks. It has remained inside the key support and resistance level of 395p and 448p since July 16. 

The stock is consolidating along the 50-day and 100-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). It is also trading at the 38.2% Fibonacci Retracement level. Also, the stock has remained inside the lower and middle lines of the Andrew’s pitchfork tool. 

Therefore, there is a likelihood that the stock will remain under pressure, potentially to the support level of 400p.

data.title: Cloudflare stock surges 20% after strong Q3 earnings: here's what analysts say
data.description:
Cloudflare shares NET surged more than 20% in premarket trading on Friday after the internet infrastructure and cybersecurity company delivered stronger-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its full-year outlook, signalling that demand for protecting digital infrastructure against emerging artificial intelligence threats is accelerating.

The rally came after the stock fell 8.3% during Thursday's regular session as cybersecurity shares came under pressure amid a broader technology market selloff.

The latest earnings report offered investors a reason to reassess the company's growth prospects, with revenue accelerating at its fastest pace in nearly four years and management highlighting rising demand from enterprise customers.

Cloudflare earnings beat estimates as AI demand accelerates

Cloudflare's third-quarter revenue increased 39% from a year earlier to $782.5 million, exceeding Wall Street's consensus estimate of $737.2 million.

Adjusted earnings came in at 38 cents per share, compared with analysts' expectations of 34 cents.

However, the company reported a net loss of $34.1 million, or 10 cents per share, compared with a loss of $1.3 million, equivalent to breakeven on a per-share basis, in the year-ago quarter.

Chief Executive Officer Matthew Prince said enterprise customer demand had accelerated during the quarter, helping the company cross $3 billion in annualised revenue.

"The third quarter was Cloudflare’s best quarter ever," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said.

"We crossed $3 billion in annualized revenue."

The company also reported strong customer additions, bringing in 308 large customers during the quarter and nearly 1,000 over the past year.

Both figures represented company records.

Cloudflare raises full-year and fourth-quarter guidance

The stronger quarterly performance prompted Cloudflare to raise its financial forecasts for the remainder of the year.

The company now expects full-year revenue of approximately $2.96 billion, compared with its previous guidance range of $2.86 billion to $2.87 billion.

Its adjusted earnings forecast was also increased to $1.35 per share from an earlier range of $1.25 to $1.26.

Analysts polled by FactSet had expected full-year revenue of $2.87 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.26 per share.

For the fourth quarter, Cloudflare projected revenue between $845 million and $846 million and adjusted earnings of 43 cents per share.

Both forecasts were comfortably above Wall Street estimates of $796 million in revenue and 38 cents in adjusted earnings per share.

Rising agentic AI traffic creates new security opportunities

Cloudflare's business involves inspecting internet traffic, helping websites load faster and protecting online infrastructure against cyber threats.

Its network also allows it to manage traffic generated by AI bots and applications.

Unlike companies that rely primarily on centralised data centres, Cloudflare operates a globally distributed network that allows it to inspect traffic and block threats closer to users.

The company argued during its earnings call that this model can be more cost-effective than the infrastructure operated by hyperscalers and neocloud providers.

The growing use of agentic AI applications is also creating additional opportunities for its security business.

The number of developers building agents on Cloudflare's Workers platform increased to 10 million in the third quarter from 7 million in the preceding quarter.

Prince said the company had also expanded its network significantly, adding approximately 5% of the entire global web since the beginning of July.

That represented a larger footprint than the combined market presence of its direct web-routing competitors, he said.

"We've partnered with nearly every major frontier AI lab and security company searching for flaws in existing software."

Cloudflare believes its security offerings are well positioned to address emerging threats as AI agents become more widely deployed.

Analysts remain divided on Cloudflare stock valuation

Analysts largely welcomed the quarterly performance, although their views on the stock's valuation varied.

Goldman Sachs reiterated its Buy rating and $420 price target following the results.

Truist Securities also maintained a Buy rating and a $350 price target.

Guggenheim raised its price target to $190 from $160, retaining its Buy rating.

The brokerage noted that few publicly traded companies are accelerating their revenue growth at Cloudflare's pace.

Jefferies, however, lowered its price target slightly to $315 from $320 while maintaining a Hold rating, citing valuation concerns despite the company beating revenue expectations by 6.2%.

Cloudflare also announced that Christian Smith would become its new president of revenue.

Smith previously worked at Cisco Systems, where he oversaw Splunk's global commercial business.

He will replace Mark Anderson, who plans to retire at the end of the year.

"Christian has consistently proven he can lead global go-to-market organizations through periods of rapid expansion with discipline, operational rigor, and a steadfast focus on customers," Prince said.

data.title: US futures mixed after Thursday's rout: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
data.description:
US markets seem set to open mixed, with Dow futures seeing a sharp decline even as the tech-heavy Nasdaq futures stage a recovery.

Nasdaq 100 futures had gained 358 points to gain 1.34% after Thursday's heavy selling and futures linked to S&P 500 were also higher.

Dow Jones Industrial Average futures, however, lost 521 points to slip over 1% and extend losses.

The Nasdaq Composite had plunged 5.52% in the previous session, marking its biggest one-day decline in 19 months and pushing the index into correction territory.

The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 3.44% to 51,523.06.

However, the tech trade at least is doing better after Thursday's rout.

Here are five things to know before US markets open on Friday, November 6, 2026

Tech and AI stocks attempt recovery

Technology and AI-related shares are bouncing in premarket trading after Thursday’s steep selloff.

Nasdaq futures rose more than 1%, while Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Broadcom and other chipmakers regained some ground.

Neoclouds, who have been under immense pressure of late, were also recovering.

The early rebound suggests some buyers are stepping in after the sharp decline, though volatility remains elevated heading into the open.

Selloff extends to Asia

Asian equities fell sharply overnight as the AI selloff spread.

South Korea’s KOSPI dropped more than 6%, extending its losses after a 5% decline in the previous session, while Japan’s Nikkei also sank.

Giants Samsung and SK Hynix led the declines.

European markets were also lower with Germany's DAX and Britain's FTSE 100 falling over 2%.

Investors are cautious after Wall Street’s technology-led rout and concerns about slower AI infrastructure spending under a Democratic Congress.

Anthropic IPO faces investor scrutiny

Major investors are questioning whether Anthropic can complete its planned initial public offering at the previously discussed $1.5 trillion valuation.

The AI company had been preparing for a listing as early as later this month. After Thursday’s broad technology selloff, some large funds now see a valuation closer to $1 trillion as more realistic.

Persuading institutional investors to take substantial exposure to the AI sector could also prove difficult so soon after they have suffered losses in the recent selloff, even if markets recover in the coming days.

Anthropic’s recent strong revenue growth remains a positive, but market conditions are clearly shifting.

Oil prices jump

Crude oil rose for a second straight session. Brent climbed above $99 a barrel and briefly topped $100 during Asian trading, while West Texas Intermediate also moved higher.

Fresh reports of tanker attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz revived supply worries amid continued uncertainty over the situation in the Middle East.

However, prices had stabilised at the time of writing, with brent around $98.5, gaining roughly 0.20% in the session. WTI crude was at $90.8 a barrel.

Jobs report in focus

The October nonfarm payrolls report is due at 8:30 AM ET. Economists expect roughly 60,000 to 65,000 new jobs, with the unemployment rate steady near 4.2%.

The data will influence the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, which currently stands at 72%.

Several companies also report results, including Moderna, Humana and Charter Communications.

The University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey follows later in the morning.

data.title: Plus500US joins TradingView for CME futures from Supercharts
data.description:
Plus500's US futures arm is now available as a broker partner on TradingView, the charting platform said on Thursday.

Eligible Plus500US clients can trade standard, E-Mini and Micro CME futures directly from TradingView's Supercharts once their accounts are connected.

The link adds another distribution route for Plus500 as it builds out regulated futures and multi-asset trading in the United States.

How the TradingView connection works

TradingView said clients connect by selecting Plus500US from the Trade button on Supercharts and signing in.

Account opening takes minutes after approval, according to the TradingView blog. There is a $0 minimum deposit.

Plus500 told TradeInformer it does not charge an extra fee for using TradingView. Clients still pay the broker's listed futures commissions and applicable exchange and National Futures Association (NFA) fees.

The integration covers Plus500US only. It is separate from Plus500's CFD and OTC retail offering outside the US.

TradingView described futures traders as one of its fastest-growing segments this year. The Plus500US listing follows other recent broker partnerships on the platform, including Mondeum Capital UK earlier in the same week, TradeInformer reported.

Commissions and what is included

Commissions are $0.49 per side for Micro contracts and $0.89 per side for standard and E-Mini contracts, excluding exchange and NFA fees, TradingView said.

Those figures match the commission table on Plus500's US futures fees page, which also lists a $10 liquidation fee per contract and an NFA regulatory fee of $0.02 per side per futures contract.

Exchange execution and clearing fees for non-members sit on top. Plus500 points clients to CME Group fee schedules for those charges.

TradeInformer noted that Plus500 still applies a $10 minimum on each payment transaction even though the account minimum deposit is zero.

Micro contracts are the smaller CME contract sizes many retail and active futures traders prefer for tighter notional exposure. The published $0.49 rate is Plus500US's commission only; all-in cost still depends on the contract and exchange fees.

Why Plus500 is pushing US distribution

Plus500 Ltd is listed on the London Stock Exchange and sits in the FTSE 250. Its US futures business combines a CFTC-regulated Futures Commission Merchant with proprietary technology, TradingView said.

The FCM lineage runs through Cunningham Commodities, which Plus500 acquired in 2021. Plus500US is a full member of CME Group and other exchanges, according to the same announcement.

The TradingView channel sits alongside Plus500's own apps as another way for approved US futures clients to send orders from charts they already use.

Secondary trade-press coverage this month has also linked Plus500's US build-out to prediction-market product steps and a planned multi-asset US offering after an agreed purchase of broker-dealer Hedge.
